obligations.statement: For all w,y, F y >= F w + dot (g w) (y-w) + (mu/2) squaredEuclideanNorm (y-w).
obligations.method: Negate the qualified scalar upper Taylor theorem; supply the actual line derivative and the proved lower curvature bound at every t. Specialize generic n,m to the bound original 4 x 80 data. Candidate proof bodies are in RealStrongLower.lean.

obligations.statement: Continuous F and Tendsto F (Filter.cocompact (Fin 80 → ℝ)) Filter.atTop.
obligations.method: Continuity follows from finite coordinate sums, exp, and Continuous.log, with 1 + exp(-dot w d) > 0 proved pointwise. Prove realPairLoss >= 0 and F w >= (mu/2) sum_j (w j)^2 from the objective itself. For each real K, put B=max 0 (2*K/mu), R=B+1. If F w <= K then (w j)^2 <= sum_j(w j)^2 <= B for every j, hence -R <= w j <= R. The sublevel {w | F w <= K} is closed and lies in the compact Pi order interval Icc (fun _ => -R) (fun _ => R). Its complement is cocompact, giving eventual K <= F w and the required Tendsto via Filter.tendsto_atTop. This uses the coordinate sum only for analytic inequalities and the product topology only for compactness.
obligations.note: Coercivity does not logically need lower_taylor; its nonnegative-loss/regularizer lemmas share the proposed first module. It is never a premise of a convergence theorem.

obligations.statement: ∃ wStar : Fin 80 → ℝ, ∀ w, F wStar <= F w.
obligations.method: Apply Continuous.exists_forall_le to the proved continuity and proved cocompact-to-atTop limit. An alternative is Continuous.exists_forall_le_of_isBounded applied to the explicitly bounded initial sublevel, but the compact Pi interval route avoids identifying the default function norm with squaredEuclideanNorm.

obligations.statement: g wStar = 0; (mu/2) squaredEuclideanNorm(w-wStar) <= F w-F wStar; the minimizer is unique.
obligations.method: For every direction v, the scalar line t ↦ F(wStar+t*v) has a global minimum at 0. Convert that actual minimum to IsLocalMin and use IsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero with the proved first derivative. Choose v=g wStar: dot(g wStar)(g wStar)=sum_j(g wStar j)^2=0, so all coordinates vanish by nonnegative finite-sum algebra. Then apply lower_taylor at wStar to obtain quadratic growth. Two global minimizers have equal F; growth and mu>0 force squared displacement 0 and coordinatewise equality.
obligations.note: Uses Fermat only on real scalar lines. No full Frechet gradient theorem or operator Hessian is required.

obligations.statement: 2*mu*(F w-F wStar) <= squaredEuclideanNorm(g w) for every w.
obligations.method: Apply lower_taylor from w to wStar. Independently prove dot(g w)v + (mu/2)sum_j(v j)^2 >= -sum_j(g w j)^2/(2*mu) by summing mu/2*(v j+g w j/mu)^2 >= 0 and field algebra using mu>0. Combine both inequalities and multiply by positive 2*mu. No assumed PL or convergence premise appears.
obligations.note: Stationarity/uniqueness are useful for final weight convergence, but not needed for this PL proof.

obligations.statement: 0 <= q < 1 and 0 <= gap (G w) <= q * gap w for every w.
obligations.method: Prove mu <= originalRealMeanL by its proved exact mu-plus-nonnegative-sum formula. Combine eta>0, mu>0, and eta*meanL<=1 to obtain eta*mu<=1, so q>=0 and q<1. Subtract F wStar from originalReal_safe_descent, multiply the derived PL inequality by eta/2>=0, and finish real arithmetic. gap>=0 follows from the proved global minimizer. All coefficients and coordinates remain the actual original model.

obligations.statement: For every w0,k, 0<=gap(W w0 k)<=q^k*gap w0; Tendsto (fun k => F(W w0 k)) atTop (nhds(F wStar)); Tendsto (W w0) atTop (nhds wStar).
obligations.method: Define the actual exact-real recurrence with Nat recursion; prove the rate by induction using the derived pointwise contraction and q>=0. Use tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one and squeeze to make the objective gap tend to zero. Quadratic growth bounds squared displacement by 2*gap/mu. Each coordinate square is at most the displacement square sum. Apply sqrt to those nonnegative scalar bounds, using Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs and Filter.Tendsto.sqrt, then squeeze each coordinate around wStar j. Assemble function-space convergence with tendsto_pi_nhds. This proves actual convergence of the exact-real fixed-data sequence without assuming any convergence or contraction statement.
